docs.title: DeepWave Module Developer Docs
docs.text: This portal provides the approved documentation set for external and internal teams that build reusable modules for the DeepWave strategy composition framework.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This site explains how to design, implement, validate, test, and maintain custom modules without exposing proprietary execution logic or operational internals. It is intentionally written around stable contracts instead of implementation details.

docs.title: Intended audience
docs.text:
• Module authors building reusable business modules.
  • Solution architects designing strategy assembly standards.
  • QA engineers validating module compatibility before release.
  • Technical writers maintaining extension documentation and templates.

docs.title: What is documented
docs.text:
• Public module contracts based on the platform module base class.
  • Supported module categories and the role of each category in a composed strategy.
  • Validation rules for module presence, ordering, and runtime suitability.
  • Configuration patterns, DSL examples, and packaging guidance.
  • Testing, debugging, and release readiness expectations.

docs.title: What is intentionally not documented
docs.text:
• Proprietary runtime orchestration and internal event choreography.
  • Broker, exchange, or execution adapter implementation details.
  • Core risk algorithms, threshold policies, or infrastructure secrets.
  • Internal service topology, credentials, or production endpoint information.

Public contract first

Treat every integration as contract-driven. If a behavior is not described in this portal or a separately approved API contract, assume it is internal and subject to change.

docs.title: Documentation map
docs.text: Section Focus Getting Started Entry path, boundaries, and workflow Architecture Safe architectural mental model for module authors Module Developer Guide Contracts, types, validation, config, examples Reference Public boundary and shared vocabulary Governance How documentation and module standards evolve

docs.title: Recommended onboarding path
docs.text:
1. Read Getting Started to understand roles, lifecycle, and non-goals.
  2. Read Public Architecture to understand where modules fit.
  3. Read Module Contract and Module Types before writing code.
  4. Use Templates and Examples to scaffold new modules safely.
  5. Complete Testing and Debugging before submission.

docs.title: Documentation principles
docs.text:
• Use explicit contracts, not tribal knowledge.
  • Prefer deterministic examples over narrative-only guidance.
  • Keep examples generic and environment-neutral.
  • Document extension points, never core implementation secrets.
  • Keep Chinese and English pages functionally equivalent.

docs.title: Architectural intent
docs.text: The module framework is designed so that strategy behavior can be assembled from reusable building blocks rather than embedded in a single monolithic strategy class. Module authors interact with a public extension layer while the platform retains control over orchestration, validation, and runtime services.

docs.title: Public architecture view
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Strategy Definition] --> B[Module Registry]
    B --> C[Validation and Preparation]
    C --> D[Execution Order Resolver]
    D --> E[Runtime Context]
    E --> F[Composed Module Chain]
    F --> G[Module Outputs]

docs.title: Module contract
docs.text: The base class defines the lifecycle, metadata, parameter validation, execution entrypoints, and metrics interface expected from every module.

docs.title: Module registry
docs.text: The registry is the controlled discovery and instantiation boundary. It resolves module classes, supports aliases, and enables dynamic loading patterns without requiring changes to the core platform.

docs.title: Validation and preparation
docs.text: Validation ensures the module set is structurally valid for the target runtime mode. Preparation can normalize order and apply approved defaults before the runtime consumes the module list.

docs.title: Runtime context
docs.text: Modules operate on a shared context object carrying market-derived data, intermediate outputs, and execution-time state exposed through the approved interface.

docs.title: Approved context allowlist
docs.text:
Module authors should only assume the following context surfaces are stable for ordinary module work:

  • market-derived data fields published through the documented context data map,
  • upstream indicator values,
  • upstream signal values,
  • module outputs written under stable module identifiers,
  • current bar or current time markers when those are surfaced by the host runtime.

Module authors should not assume direct ownership of broker handles, transport objects, internal validation flags, or host-managed runtime state unless a separate contract explicitly grants access.

docs.title: Design constraints for module authors
docs.text:
• Keep module logic business-focused.
  • Do not assume direct access to internal infrastructure services.
  • Do not hardcode environment-specific execution details.
  • Do not rely on undocumented sequencing side effects.
  • Treat the context as a shared integration surface, not a dumping ground.

docs.title: Dependency injection guidance
docs.text: The platform uses a dependency injection model for infrastructure services. Module authors should depend on constructor input, context input, or approved configuration, not on container internals. When a test requires substitutes, use mocks and provider overrides in the consuming application or test harness, not inside the module itself.

docs.title: Safe architecture boundary
docs.text:
The following are appropriate to reference in external developer docs:

  • module categories,
  • ordering rules,
  • lifecycle methods,
  • metadata and schema responsibilities,
  • composition-safe examples.

The following are not appropriate:

  • internal event bus implementation,
  • execution adapter topology,
  • live trading state synchronization internals,
  • backend integration secrets.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The platform supports composition-based strategy development. A strategy is assembled from independently authored modules, each with a clear responsibility, a declared type, and validated parameters.

This documentation is for developers creating modules that operate within that composition model. It does not describe the platform's proprietary trading internals.

docs.title: Development model
docs.text:
Module development follows a contract-first workflow:

  1. Select the target module category.
  2. Implement the required module contract.
  3. Declare metadata and parameter schema.
  4. Validate ordering and composition assumptions.
  5. Test in isolated and composed scenarios.
  6. Publish documentation and usage examples with the module.

docs.title: Safe mental model
docs.text:
You can think of the platform as a composition runtime that:

  • accepts a list of modules,
  • validates structural correctness,
  • executes modules in an approved order,
  • shares a controlled context object, and
  • captures outputs for downstream modules.

The exact internals behind orchestration, transport, execution backends, and system-wide risk services are outside the scope of module author documentation.

docs.title: Stable source contracts
docs.text:
The current approved authoring model is derived from the platform's stable public contracts and validation layers, including:

  • ModuleBase
  • ModuleRegistry
  • StrategyValidator
  • StrategyPreparer
  • ModuleExecutionOrder
  • platform-level module configuration models

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
This portal does not attempt to explain:

  • order routing or broker connectivity,
  • exchange adapter behavior,
  • internal risk engine formulas,
  • infrastructure deployment internals, or
  • production environment operations.

docs.title: Definition of a production-ready module
docs.text:
A production-ready module must:

  • implement the declared contract correctly,
  • validate its input parameters,
  • avoid hidden external dependencies,
  • remain deterministic under repeated execution,
  • document assumptions and outputs,
  • include tests and troubleshooting guidance.

docs.title: Governance objective
docs.text: Enterprise documentation is part of the module delivery standard. A module is not complete unless its documentation, examples, and test evidence are aligned.

docs.title: Required contribution package
docs.text:
Every new module contribution should include:

  • implementation code,
  • tests,
  • parameter reference,
  • one usage example,
  • troubleshooting notes,
  • boundary review if a new capability is introduced.

docs.title: Documentation review criteria
docs.text:
Reviewers should confirm:

  • the module category is correct,
  • public terminology is consistent,
  • examples are safe and environment-neutral,
  • no internal or proprietary details are exposed,
  • English and Chinese pages remain aligned where required.

docs.title: Minor change
docs.text: Examples: typo fixes, clarifications, non-breaking example updates.

docs.title: Contract-affecting change
docs.text:
Examples: parameter rename, output shape change, lifecycle expectation change, new approved module type.

Contract-affecting changes require coordinated updates to tests, examples, and both language versions of the docs.

docs.title: Recommended publication flow
docs.text:
1. Draft the module and reference doc.
  2. Complete unit, contract, and composition tests.
  3. Perform boundary review.
  4. Update both language trees.
  5. Build the static site and verify links.
  6. Publish with release notes if the contract changed.

docs.title: Configuration philosophy
docs.text: The platform favors typed, validated, configuration-driven composition. Module authors should expose stable parameters and keep environment-specific concerns outside the module implementation.

docs.title: Module-level parameters
docs.text: Each module owns its own parameter contract through params_schema and semantic validation.

docs.title: Platform module configuration
docs.text: The wider platform also uses typed configuration models for shared module settings and strategy assembly. Module developers should align naming, defaults, and data types with those platform conventions without depending on internal subsystem details.

docs.title: Example strategy composition
docs.text:
strategy:
  name: trend_following_reference
  modules:
    - type: indicator
      name: moving_average_fast
      params:
        lookback: 20
    - type: indicator
      name: moving_average_slow
      params:
        lookback: 50
    - type: signal
      name: crossover_signal
      params:
        fast_ref: moving_average_fast
        slow_ref: moving_average_slow
    - type: risk
      name: volatility_guard
      params:
        max_volatility: 0.18
    - type: position
      name: directional_position
      params:
        mode: long_short
    - type: execution
      name: simulated_execution
      params:
        timeout_ms: 5000

docs.title: Parameter design rules
docs.text:
• Use explicit names.
  • Use bounded numeric values where possible.
  • Prefer primitive types and small structured objects.
  • Separate tuning parameters from environment configuration.
  • Document defaults and failure conditions.

docs.title: Example parameter table
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description lookback integer Yes Number of prior observations used threshold float No Decision sensitivity, usually bounded mode string No Named operating mode

docs.title: DSL authoring guidance
docs.text: If your team maintains a strategy DSL or generated config format, keep the module-facing part stable and declarative. A module should be configurable without requiring authors to know anything about private runtime services.

docs.title: Configuration anti-patterns
docs.text:
• embedding hostnames, credentials, or secrets in module examples,
  • reusing one parameter for multiple unrelated meanings,
  • relying on undocumented implicit defaults,
  • exposing internal adapter settings as public module parameters.

docs.title: Core contract
docs.text: Every custom module must inherit from the platform base contract and supply a predictable set of metadata and behaviors.

docs.title: Required contract elements
docs.text: Element Responsibility name Public module identifier version Contracted module version type Declared module category description Human-readable purpose params_schema Parameter schema used for validation validate_params Semantic parameter validation init One-time initialization next_async Main execution entrypoint

docs.title: Optional contract elements
docs.text:
Element Use aliases Backward-compatible or alternate names tick_update Forming-bar or tick-level update logic on_error Custom error handling hook get_metrics Module metrics surface get_metadata Metadata export

Restricted host hooks

Host-side result handling extensions are not part of the standard external module contract. Do not design a third-party module around unpublished host hooks unless your team has explicit approval.

docs.title: Lifecycle overview
docs.text:
1. Parameters are validated at construction time.
  2. The runtime assigns or resolves the module identifier.
  3. init is called once before regular execution begins.
  4. next_async is called for normal module execution.
  5. tick_update may be called for modules that support incremental updates.
  6. Errors may flow through on_error if the runtime chooses to surface them there.

docs.title: Keep validation layered
docs.text: Use params_schema for structural validation and validate_params for semantic validation. A schema should ensure shape and type. Semantic validation should ensure business correctness such as positive lookback windows, bounded thresholds, or valid field relationships.

docs.title: Keep initialization light
docs.text: init should prepare module state only. Avoid network calls, file system writes, or heavyweight runtime coupling.

docs.title: Prefer async-native logic
docs.text: Implement next_async as the source of truth. The sync wrapper exists for compatibility but should not be treated as the primary extension model.

docs.title: Minimal template
docs.text:
from typing import Any, Dict

from src.strategy_modules.core.module_base import BacktestContext, ModuleBase, ModuleType


class ExampleSignal(ModuleBase):
    name = "example_signal"
    version = "1.0.0"
    type = ModuleType.SIGNAL
    description = "Reference signal module"
    params_schema = {
        "lookback": {"type": "int", "required": True},
        "threshold": {"type": "float", "required": True},
    }

    def validate_params(self, params: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
        return params["lookback"] > 0 and 0.0 <= params["threshold"] <= 1.0

    def init(self, bt_ctx: BacktestContext) -> None:
        self.last_value = None

    async def next_async(self, bt_ctx: BacktestContext) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        value = bt_ctx.indicators.get("reference_indicator")
        self.last_value = value
        return {"signal": "hold", "value": value}

docs.title: Documentation expectations for each module
docs.text:
Every module package should ship with:

  • module purpose and category,
  • parameter table,
  • output contract,
  • compatibility assumptions,
  • example configuration,
  • known failure modes.

docs.title: Supported categories
docs.text:
The platform currently exposes the following module categories through the public base contract.

Type Purpose Typical output indicator Computes derived values from market data or context Numeric or structured indicator values signal Produces directional or stateful trade intent Signal state, confidence, rationale filter Refines, suppresses, or qualifies signal flow Pass or block decisions risk Evaluates trade or position risk constraints Risk assessment or constraints sizer Determines exposure or quantity sizing Size recommendation position Produces position-level action decisions Open, close, hold, reduce execution Bridges position intent into an execution-compatible action Execution payload or accepted action output Emits reporting, logging, or derived records Output artifacts portfolio Computes portfolio-level aggregation or overlay behavior Portfolio metrics or directives

docs.title: Indicator modules
docs.text: Use indicator modules for deterministic transformations. They should avoid side effects and focus on producing reusable values for downstream modules.

docs.title: Signal modules
docs.text: Signal modules should explain the decision state clearly. Prefer explicit structured outputs over opaque booleans when downstream traceability matters.

docs.title: Filter modules
docs.text: Filters are best when they are composable and transparent. Document the exact blocking conditions and how they interact with missing inputs.

docs.title: Risk modules
docs.text: Custom risk modules may express local, strategy-specific checks, but they must not attempt to reproduce platform-level system risk internals.

docs.title: Sizer and position modules
docs.text: These modules should separate quantity decisions from directional decisions whenever possible. That makes strategies easier to reason about and validate.

docs.title: Execution modules
docs.text: Execution modules are a controlled extension point. Treat them as approval-based capabilities, not the default path for third-party module work. Keep them generic, configuration-driven, and abstracted from infrastructure secrets.

docs.title: Output and portfolio modules
docs.text: These modules should remain observational or aggregative. Avoid embedding control flow that surprises upstream business logic.

docs.title: Category selection checklist
docs.text:
• If it derives a value from data, it is probably an indicator.
  • If it decides trade intent, it is probably a signal or position module.
  • If it approves or rejects an action, it is probably a filter or risk module.
  • If it determines quantity, it is a sizer.
  • If it bridges intent into execution-ready action, it is an execution module.
  • If it records or aggregates, it is an output or portfolio module.

docs.title: Recommended module package structure
docs.text:
my-module-package/
  README.md
  module.py
  tests/
    test_module.py
    test_integration_contract.py
  docs/
    module-reference.md

docs.title: Indicator template
docs.text:
class ExampleIndicator(ModuleBase):
    name = "example_indicator"
    version = "1.0.0"
    type = ModuleType.INDICATOR
    description = "Computes a rolling value for downstream modules"
    params_schema = {"lookback": {"type": "int", "required": True}}

    def validate_params(self, params):
        return params["lookback"] > 1

    def init(self, bt_ctx):
        self.history = []

    async def next_async(self, bt_ctx):
        price = bt_ctx.data.get("close")
        self.history.append(price)
        value = sum(self.history[-self.params["lookback"]:]) / self.params["lookback"]
        bt_ctx.indicators[self.module_id] = value
        bt_ctx.module_outputs[self.module_id] = value
        return value

docs.title: Signal template
docs.text:
class ExampleSignal(ModuleBase):
    name = "example_signal"
    version = "1.0.0"
    type = ModuleType.SIGNAL
    description = "Turns indicator state into a normalized signal"
    params_schema = {"indicator_ref": {"type": "str", "required": True}}

    def validate_params(self, params):
        return bool(params["indicator_ref"])

    def init(self, bt_ctx):
        self.last_signal = "hold"

    async def next_async(self, bt_ctx):
        value = bt_ctx.indicators.get(self.params["indicator_ref"])
        signal = "buy" if value else "hold"
        result = {"signal": signal, "source": self.params["indicator_ref"]}
        bt_ctx.signals[self.module_id] = result
        bt_ctx.module_outputs[self.module_id] = result
        return result

docs.title: Output and reference contract
docs.text:
When a module publishes values for downstream use, follow these rules:

  1. Write outputs using the module's stable module_id.
  2. Use one documented output shape per version.
  3. Prefer explicit references such as indicator_ref, signal_ref, or similarly named parameters over positional assumptions.
  4. Document whether the module writes into shared indicator or signal maps, general module outputs, or both.
  5. If downstream modules depend on a specific field, publish that field name in the module reference.

docs.title: Documentation template for every module
docs.text:
Use this structure in the module-specific README or reference page:

  1. Module summary.
  2. Category and dependencies.
  3. Parameter table.
  4. Input assumptions.
  5. Output contract.
  6. Failure modes.
  7. Compatibility notes.
  8. Example strategy usage.

docs.title: Example release checklist
docs.text:
• contract methods implemented,
  • parameter validation present,
  • deterministic example config provided,
  • unit and contract tests passing,
  • bilingual documentation prepared if required by your program.

docs.title: Testing strategy
docs.text: Every module should be verified at three levels.

docs.title: Unit tests
docs.text: Validate parameter handling, pure logic, boundary conditions, and deterministic outputs.

docs.title: Contract tests
docs.text:
Verify the module behaves correctly against the public platform contract:

  • correct type,
  • valid metadata,
  • expected output structure,
  • safe handling of missing context values,
  • no forbidden side effects in normal execution.

docs.title: Composition tests
docs.text: Run the module inside a realistic module chain with upstream and downstream dependencies represented by test doubles or lightweight reference modules.

docs.title: Recommended pytest structure
docs.text:
tests/
  test_params.py
  test_lifecycle.py
  test_outputs.py
  test_composition.py

docs.title: Debugging guidance
docs.text:
• Inspect module inputs before changing business logic.
  • Confirm upstream module identifiers match configuration references.
  • Check ordering and runtime mode assumptions first.
  • Reproduce with the smallest valid composition.
  • Record module output shape changes in docs and tests together.

docs.title: Failure triage table
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause First check Module fails at creation Invalid params Schema and semantic validation Output missing downstream Wrong module id or missing context write module_id and output mapping Composition rejected Ordering or required type violation Validation rules Behavior differs by mode Unsupported execution assumption Runtime compatibility note

docs.title: Logging guidance
docs.text: Prefer structured, contextual diagnostics in the host application. A module should expose enough state for diagnosis without coupling itself to a specific logging backend.

docs.title: Release gate
docs.text: Do not publish a module unless its tests, examples, and documentation agree on the same parameter names, outputs, and compatibility assumptions.

docs.title: Why validation exists
docs.text: The platform validates module composition before runtime so that structural errors are caught early and consistently.

docs.title: Canonical ordering
docs.text:
The approved execution order is:

  1. indicator
  2. signal
  3. filter
  4. risk
  5. position
  6. execution
  7. output
  8. portfolio

This order reflects dependency flow from derived data to decisioning, action shaping, execution bridging, and reporting.

docs.title: Live-oriented composition
docs.text:
The validated live composition requires:

  • at least one indicator module,
  • at least one signal module,
  • at least one position module,
  • exactly one execution module,
  • execution placed after position modules,
  • no ordering violations.

docs.title: Backtest-oriented composition
docs.text: Backtest composition still requires valid ordering. If an execution module is present, it must be a simulation-safe execution variant approved for non-live use.

docs.title: Preparation behavior
docs.text: Before validation completes, the preparation layer may sort modules into canonical order and may add an execution module through approved platform defaults. Module authors must not rely on those defaults. Always document the expected full module set in examples.

docs.title: Failure patterns to avoid
docs.text:
• placing a filter before its required signal producer,
  • assuming position logic can run before indicator calculations,
  • defining multiple execution modules in one composition,
  • omitting a position module from a live composition,
  • using production-specific execution assumptions in backtest examples.

docs.title: Review checklist
docs.text:
Before releasing a module, verify:

  • the module type matches its actual responsibility,
  • the example strategy order is canonical,
  • required upstream inputs are listed,
  • missing-input behavior is documented,
  • runtime mode compatibility is explicit.

docs.title: Core terms
docs.text: Module A reusable strategy building block implementing the platform contract. Module type The declared category that determines the module's role in composition and validation. Context The shared runtime object carrying current data, intermediate values, and outputs between modules. Composition An ordered list of modules assembled into one strategy definition. Registry The discovery and resolution boundary responsible for locating and instantiating module classes. Preparation The normalization step that can reorder modules or apply approved defaults before validation completes. Validation Structural and semantic checks ensuring a module set is safe and compatible with the target runtime mode. Runtime mode The target execution context, such as live-oriented or backtest-oriented operation. Contract test A test that verifies a module conforms to the public extension surface rather than only its own internal logic. Public API boundary The set of approved contracts and behaviors safe to expose to external module developers.

docs.title: Boundary statement
docs.text: This portal documents only the approved extension surface for module developers. Everything outside this surface must be treated as internal unless separately approved.

docs.title: Base module contract
docs.text:
The public contract includes:

  • module metadata fields,
  • parameter schema conventions,
  • lifecycle methods,
  • metrics and metadata accessors,
  • shared context usage patterns.

docs.title: Registry-facing concepts
docs.text:
The public model includes:

  • registration,
  • alias support,
  • discovery and resolution concepts,
  • safe instantiation expectations.

docs.title: Author-facing discovery rules
docs.text:
• Module names must be stable, human-readable, and safe to reference from configuration.
  • Aliases are a compatibility tool, not a naming shortcut. When an alias is introduced, the canonical name must remain documented.
  • A module is considered discoverable only when it is packaged and exposed through an approved registration or discovery path in the host application.
  • Dynamic discovery behavior may vary by deployment. Module authors must not assume every environment enables automatic discovery.

docs.title: Identifier and output rules
docs.text:
• module_id should remain stable within a strategy definition.
  • Outputs intended for downstream consumption must be written under deterministic keys.
  • Downstream references such as indicator_ref or similar pointers must target documented module identifiers, not implicit ordering.
  • If a module changes its output shape, that is a contract change and must be versioned and documented.

docs.title: Validation-facing concepts
docs.text:
The public model includes:

  • canonical ordering,
  • live and backtest composition expectations,
  • preparation concepts that affect documentation and examples.

docs.title: Controlled extension areas
docs.text: Execution-oriented extensions are not a default public customization path. They are controlled capabilities with stronger review, validation, and runtime constraints than ordinary indicator, signal, filter, risk, sizer, position, output, or portfolio modules.

docs.title: Internal-only areas
docs.text:
The following topics are intentionally excluded from this site:

  • proprietary execution flow internals,
  • infrastructure container implementation details,
  • live adapter protocols,
  • state persistence mechanisms,
  • system-wide risk enforcement logic,
  • operational thresholds and production tuning.

docs.title: How to request a boundary change
docs.text:
If a module team needs a currently internal capability to become public, open a documentation governance request that includes:

  1. use case,
  2. proposed contract,
  3. security and stability considerations,
  4. backward compatibility expectations.

No team should publish internal code excerpts as external guidance without approval.

docs.title: DeepWave 模块开发者文档
docs.text: 本门户提供面向外部与内部模块开发团队的正式文档集，用于指导开发可复用的策略模块，并确保开发过程遵循平台公开契约而不是依赖内部实现细节。

docs.title: 文档目标
docs.text: 本网站说明如何设计、实现、校验、测试和维护自定义模块，同时明确哪些内容属于平台内部能力，不能作为外部开发依赖。

docs.title: 适用对象
docs.text:
• 开发指标、信号、过滤、风险、仓位、执行等模块的工程师。
  • 负责策略组合规范的架构师。
  • 负责模块验收与兼容性验证的 QA 团队。
  • 负责维护扩展文档模板和标准的技术写作者。

docs.title: 文档覆盖范围
docs.text:
• 模块基类所定义的公开契约。
  • 组合式策略中支持的模块类型及职责边界。
  • 模块校验规则、排序规则与运行模式兼容性。
  • 配置模式、DSL 示例、测试要求与发布清单。

docs.title: 明确不公开的内容
docs.text:
• 平台内部执行编排与事件链路实现。
  • 经纪商、交易适配器、执行后端的内部细节。
  • 核心风险算法、阈值策略、基础设施秘密信息。
  • 生产环境拓扑、凭据、真实接口地址。

以公开契约为准

如果某个行为没有在本门户或单独批准的 API 契约中说明，就应视为内部实现，不应作为模块开发依赖。

docs.title: 文档结构
docs.text: 栏目 内容 快速开始 角色、边界与开发路径 架构说明 面向模块作者的安全架构视图 模块开发指南 契约、类型、校验、配置、示例 参考资料 公开边界与统一术语 文档治理 文档和模块标准如何演进

docs.title: 建议阅读顺序
docs.text:
1. 先阅读“快速开始”，理解本门户的边界与非目标。
  2. 再阅读“公开架构”，建立正确的系统心智模型。
  3. 在写代码前阅读“模块契约”和“模块类型”。
  4. 使用“模板与示例”作为脚手架。
  5. 提交前完成“测试与调试”中的检查项。

docs.title: 文档原则
docs.text:
• 使用显式契约，而不是依赖口口相传的经验；
  • 优先给出可复现示例，而不是只有叙述；
  • 示例必须保持通用且与环境无关；
  • 只记录扩展点，不泄露核心实现秘密；
  • 中英文页面在能力和约束上必须保持等价。

docs.title: 架构意图
docs.text: 模块框架的核心目标，是让策略能力通过多个可复用积木拼装出来，而不是集中写在一个巨大的策略类里。模块作者只需要面向扩展层开发，平台继续掌控编排、校验和运行期服务。

docs.title: 面向开发者的安全架构视图
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[策略定义] --> B[模块注册中心]
    B --> C[校验与准备]
    C --> D[执行顺序解析]
    D --> E[运行时上下文]
    E --> F[组合模块链]
    F --> G[模块输出]

docs.title: 模块契约
docs.text: 模块基类定义了生命周期、元数据、参数校验、执行入口和指标接口，是所有模块开发的基础。

docs.title: 模块注册中心
docs.text: 注册中心是受控的发现与实例化边界。它负责模块解析、别名支持和动态加载能力，使得扩展模块可以接入平台，而无需修改平台核心代码。

docs.title: 校验与准备层
docs.text: 校验负责确认模块集合对目标运行模式是结构正确的。准备层可以在进入运行时之前做顺序标准化以及批准范围内的默认补全。

docs.title: 运行时上下文
docs.text: 模块通过共享上下文访问市场数据、上游输出和当前执行态。模块作者应把它当作受控接口，而不是内部系统总线。

docs.title: 作者可依赖的上下文 allowlist
docs.text:
普通模块开发只应稳定依赖以下上下文表面：

  • 文档化的数据映射中发布的市场派生数据；
  • 上游指标结果；
  • 上游信号结果；
  • 通过稳定模块标识写入的模块输出；
  • 宿主运行时显式暴露的当前 bar 或当前时间标记。

除非另有明确契约，不应假设自己可以直接拥有 broker 句柄、传输对象、内部校验标志或宿主管理的运行时状态。

docs.title: 模块作者的设计约束
docs.text:
• 模块逻辑应聚焦业务职责。
  • 不要假设可以直接访问内部基础设施服务。
  • 不要把环境细节硬编码到模块中。
  • 不要依赖未文档化的顺序副作用。
  • 不要把上下文当成随意写入的全局存储。

docs.title: 依赖注入建议
docs.text: 平台整体使用依赖注入管理基础设施，但模块作者不应依赖容器内部结构。若测试需要替身，应在宿主应用或测试装配层完成 provider override，而不是在模块内直接绑死容器实现。

docs.title: 安全边界
docs.text:
适合对外公开的内容包括：

  • 模块类型与职责；
  • 排序规则；
  • 生命周期方法；
  • 元数据与参数模式职责；
  • 不涉及内部细节的组合示例。

不适合对外公开的内容包括：

  • 事件总线内部实现；
  • 执行适配器拓扑；
  • 实盘状态同步内部链路；
  • 后端集成秘密信息。

docs.title: 范围说明
docs.text:
该平台采用组合式策略开发模式。一个策略由多个职责清晰、参数可校验、类型已声明的模块组合而成。

本套文档仅面向模块开发者，帮助你在公开边界内构建新模块，而不是解释平台专有的交易内部实现。

docs.title: 开发流程
docs.text:
模块开发遵循契约优先的路径：

  1. 选择目标模块类型。
  2. 按模块基类实现必要方法。
  3. 声明元数据与参数模式。
  4. 核对排序和组合约束。
  5. 在隔离场景和组合场景中测试。
  6. 随模块一起交付文档和示例。

docs.title: 建议心智模型
docs.text:
可以把平台理解为一个组合运行时，它会：

  • 接收按顺序定义的模块列表；
  • 在运行前做结构性校验；
  • 根据批准顺序执行模块；
  • 通过受控上下文共享数据与输出；
  • 保存模块产出供下游模块消费。

至于内部编排、执行后端、系统级风控与基础设施服务，这些不属于模块作者需要依赖的知识范围。

docs.title: 公开事实来源
docs.text:
本门户当前依据平台稳定的公开契约与校验层进行抽象，包括：

  • ModuleBase
  • ModuleRegistry
  • StrategyValidator
  • StrategyPreparer
  • ModuleExecutionOrder
  • 平台级模块配置模型

docs.title: 非目标
docs.text:
本门户不解释以下内容：

  • 下单路由和经纪商连接；
  • 交易所或执行适配器内部行为；
  • 平台核心风险算法；
  • 生产基础设施与运维细节。

docs.title: 生产级模块的标准
docs.text:
一个可发布的模块至少应满足：

  • 正确实现公开契约；
  • 对参数进行结构和语义校验；
  • 不依赖隐式外部环境；
  • 在重复执行下具有可预测行为；
  • 具备参数说明、输出说明、测试与故障说明。

docs.title: 治理目标
docs.text: 企业级文档是模块交付标准的一部分。一个模块如果没有与代码、示例、测试一致的文档，就不算完整交付。

docs.title: 必须一起提交的内容
docs.text:
每一个新模块贡献至少应包含：

  • 实现代码；
  • 测试；
  • 参数参考；
  • 一个使用示例；
  • 故障说明；
  • 如果引入新能力，还要完成边界评审。

docs.title: 文档评审标准
docs.text:
评审人应确认：

  • 模块类型是否正确；
  • 公开术语是否一致；
  • 示例是否安全且不绑定环境；
  • 是否泄露内部或专有细节；
  • 如果项目要求双语，中英文页面是否保持等价。

docs.title: 小变更
docs.text: 例如错别字、表述优化、非破坏性示例更新。

docs.title: 契约变更
docs.text:
例如参数改名、输出结构变化、生命周期预期变化、新增批准模块类型。

契约变更必须同步更新测试、示例以及两个语言版本的文档。

docs.title: 建议发布流程
docs.text:
1. 起草模块与参考文档；
  2. 完成单元测试、契约测试和组合测试；
  3. 完成公开边界审查；
  4. 更新中英文文档；
  5. 构建静态站点并检查链接；
  6. 如果契约变化，对外附带发布说明。

docs.title: 配置哲学
docs.text: 平台采用类型化、可校验、配置驱动的组合方式。模块作者应暴露稳定参数，并将环境细节与模块逻辑分离。

docs.title: 模块参数层
docs.text: 每个模块通过 params_schema 和语义校验函数定义自己的参数契约。

docs.title: 平台模块配置层
docs.text: 平台整体还定义了用于共享模块设置和策略装配的类型化配置模型。模块作者应尽量与这些既有约定在命名、默认值和数据类型上保持一致，但不应依赖内部子系统细节。

docs.title: 策略组合示例
docs.text:
strategy:
  name: trend_following_reference
  modules:
    - type: indicator
      name: moving_average_fast
      params:
        lookback: 20
    - type: indicator
      name: moving_average_slow
      params:
        lookback: 50
    - type: signal
      name: crossover_signal
      params:
        fast_ref: moving_average_fast
        slow_ref: moving_average_slow
    - type: risk
      name: volatility_guard
      params:
        max_volatility: 0.18
    - type: position
      name: directional_position
      params:
        mode: long_short
    - type: execution
      name: simulated_execution
      params:
        timeout_ms: 5000

docs.title: 参数设计规则
docs.text:
• 参数名要明确；
  • 数值参数尽量有边界；
  • 优先使用简单类型和小型结构；
  • 调优参数与环境配置分离；
  • 默认值和失败条件必须写清楚。

docs.title: 参数表模板
docs.text: 参数 类型 必填 说明 lookback integer 是 使用的历史观测数量 threshold float 否 决策灵敏度，通常应有边界 mode string 否 命名化运行模式

docs.title: DSL 编写建议
docs.text: 如果团队维护自己的策略 DSL 或配置生成器，模块面对开发者的部分应保持稳定、声明式。模块应能在不知道任何内部基础设施实现的前提下完成配置。

docs.title: 配置反模式
docs.text:
• 在模块示例中写入主机、密钥或凭据；
  • 一个参数承担多个含义；
  • 依赖未写入文档的隐式默认值；
  • 把内部适配器参数暴露为公开模块参数。

docs.title: 核心要求
docs.text: 每一个自定义模块都必须继承平台模块基类，并提供一致、可预测的元数据和行为接口。

docs.title: 必要契约元素
docs.text: 元素 责任 name 模块公开标识符 version 模块版本 type 模块类型声明 description 模块用途说明 params_schema 参数结构定义 validate_params 参数语义校验 init 一次性初始化 next_async 主执行入口

docs.title: 可选契约元素
docs.text:
元素 用途 aliases 向后兼容或别名能力 tick_update Tick 或 forming bar 更新逻辑 on_error 自定义错误钩子 get_metrics 暴露模块指标 get_metadata 导出元数据

受限宿主钩子

宿主侧结果处理扩展不属于标准外部模块契约。除非经过明确批准，不要让第三方模块依赖任何未公开的宿主钩子。

docs.title: 生命周期概览
docs.text:
1. 构造模块时先做参数校验。
  2. 平台为模块分配或解析模块标识。
  3. init 在正式执行前调用一次。
  4. next_async 作为主要运行入口被调用。
  5. 如果模块支持 Tick 级别更新，运行时可能调用 tick_update。
  6. 错误在某些场景下会流经 on_error。

docs.title: 参数校验要分层
docs.text: params_schema 负责结构层校验，validate_params 负责业务语义校验。结构层解决字段、类型、是否必填，语义层解决取值范围、组合关系和业务合法性。

docs.title: 初始化要轻量
docs.text: init 应只负责准备模块状态，不应在这里做网络调用、文件写入或重型环境绑定。

docs.title: 以异步实现为主
docs.text: 推荐把 next_async 作为真实逻辑来源。同步入口主要用于兼容，不应成为首选扩展模型。

docs.title: 最小实现模板
docs.text:
from typing import Any, Dict

from src.strategy_modules.core.module_base import BacktestContext, ModuleBase, ModuleType


class ExampleSignal(ModuleBase):
    name = "example_signal"
    version = "1.0.0"
    type = ModuleType.SIGNAL
    description = "参考信号模块"
    params_schema = {
        "lookback": {"type": "int", "required": True},
        "threshold": {"type": "float", "required": True},
    }

    def validate_params(self, params: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
        return params["lookback"] > 0 and 0.0 <= params["threshold"] <= 1.0

    def init(self, bt_ctx: BacktestContext) -> None:
        self.last_value = None

    async def next_async(self, bt_ctx: BacktestContext) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        value = bt_ctx.indicators.get("reference_indicator")
        self.last_value = value
        return {"signal": "hold", "value": value}

docs.title: 每个模块必须附带的文档
docs.text:
• 模块作用与所属类型；
  • 参数表；
  • 输入假设；
  • 输出契约；
  • 失败场景；
  • 配置示例；
  • 兼容性说明。

docs.title: 支持的模块类别
docs.text:
当前平台通过公开模块基类暴露以下模块类别。

类型 作用 常见输出 indicator 从市场数据或上下文推导衍生值 数值或结构化指标结果 signal 生成交易意图或状态判断 信号状态、置信度、原因 filter 对信号进行筛选、抑制或限定 通过或阻断决策 risk 评估交易或仓位风险约束 风险结论或限制条件 sizer 决定暴露规模或数量 仓位大小建议 position 生成仓位层面的动作决策 开仓、平仓、持有、减仓 execution 将仓位意图转换为可执行动作 执行负载或动作请求 output 输出记录、报表或衍生结果 输出产物 portfolio 做组合级聚合或叠加处理 组合指标或组合指令

docs.title: 指标模块
docs.text: 应尽量保持纯计算和无副作用，为下游模块稳定提供可复用数值。

docs.title: 信号模块
docs.text: 建议输出结构化结果，而不是只返回布尔值，这有助于下游模块追踪来源和原因。

docs.title: 过滤模块
docs.text: 过滤模块要特别注意透明性，必须明确阻断条件以及在输入缺失时的行为。

docs.title: 风险模块
docs.text: 自定义风险模块可以表达策略局部约束，但不应试图复刻平台系统级风险内部能力。

docs.title: Sizer 与 Position 模块
docs.text: 数量决策和方向决策最好拆开，这样组合验证与测试都更容易。

docs.title: 执行模块
docs.text: 执行模块属于受控的高级扩展点，不应被视为普通第三方模块开发的默认路径。它应保持通用、参数驱动，并与基础设施秘密隔离。

docs.title: Output 与 Portfolio 模块
docs.text: 建议保持观测性或聚合性，不要引入让上游业务逻辑难以理解的隐藏控制流。

docs.title: 类型选择检查表
docs.text:
• 如果主要职责是计算值，大概率属于指标模块。
  • 如果主要职责是给出交易意图，大概率属于信号或仓位模块。
  • 如果主要职责是批准或否决动作，大概率属于过滤或风险模块。
  • 如果主要职责是决定数量，它就是 sizer。
  • 如果主要职责是把意图桥接为执行动作，它就是执行模块。
  • 如果主要职责是记录或聚合，它更可能属于 output 或 portfolio 模块。

docs.title: 推荐模块包结构
docs.text:
my-module-package/
  README.md
  module.py
  tests/
    test_module.py
    test_integration_contract.py
  docs/
    module-reference.md

docs.title: 指标模块模板
docs.text:
class ExampleIndicator(ModuleBase):
    name = "example_indicator"
    version = "1.0.0"
    type = ModuleType.INDICATOR
    description = "为下游模块计算滚动值"
    params_schema = {"lookback": {"type": "int", "required": True}}

    def validate_params(self, params):
        return params["lookback"] > 1

    def init(self, bt_ctx):
        self.history = []

    async def next_async(self, bt_ctx):
        price = bt_ctx.data.get("close")
        self.history.append(price)
        value = sum(self.history[-self.params["lookback"]:]) / self.params["lookback"]
        bt_ctx.indicators[self.module_id] = value
        bt_ctx.module_outputs[self.module_id] = value
        return value

docs.title: 信号模块模板
docs.text:
class ExampleSignal(ModuleBase):
    name = "example_signal"
    version = "1.0.0"
    type = ModuleType.SIGNAL
    description = "把指标状态转换成标准化信号"
    params_schema = {"indicator_ref": {"type": "str", "required": True}}

    def validate_params(self, params):
        return bool(params["indicator_ref"])

    def init(self, bt_ctx):
        self.last_signal = "hold"

    async def next_async(self, bt_ctx):
        value = bt_ctx.indicators.get(self.params["indicator_ref"])
        signal = "buy" if value else "hold"
        result = {"signal": signal, "source": self.params["indicator_ref"]}
        bt_ctx.signals[self.module_id] = result
        bt_ctx.module_outputs[self.module_id] = result
        return result

docs.title: 输出与引用契约
docs.text:
当模块要把结果提供给下游消费时，遵循以下规则：

  1. 使用稳定的 module_id 写入输出；
  2. 每个版本只维护一种文档化输出结构；
  3. 优先使用 indicator_ref、signal_ref 等显式引用，不要依赖位置顺序；
  4. 明确说明模块会写入指标映射、信号映射、通用模块输出，还是同时写入多个表面；
  5. 如果下游依赖某个具体字段，必须在模块参考文档中公开该字段名。

docs.title: 每个模块建议采用的文档模板
docs.text:
1. 模块摘要；
  2. 所属类型与依赖；
  3. 参数表；
  4. 输入假设；
  5. 输出契约；
  6. 失败模式；
  7. 兼容性说明；
  8. 策略使用示例。

docs.title: 发布清单
docs.text:
• 契约方法已实现；
  • 参数校验存在；
  • 提供可复现配置示例；
  • 单元测试和契约测试通过；
  • 如果项目要求双语，则中英文文档齐全。

docs.title: 测试策略
docs.text: 每个模块至少应在三个层面得到验证。

docs.title: 单元测试
docs.text: 验证参数处理、纯逻辑、边界条件和确定性输出。

docs.title: 契约测试
docs.text:
确认模块符合公开平台契约：

  • type 是否正确；
  • 元数据是否完整；
  • 输出结构是否符合约定；
  • 输入缺失时是否安全；
  • 正常执行时是否没有禁止的副作用。

docs.title: 组合测试
docs.text: 把模块放进一个真实的模块链里进行验证，上下游依赖可以由测试替身或轻量参考模块提供。

docs.title: 推荐的 pytest 结构
docs.text:
tests/
  test_params.py
  test_lifecycle.py
  test_outputs.py
  test_composition.py

docs.title: 调试建议
docs.text:
• 修改业务逻辑前先确认输入是否正确；
  • 先检查上游模块标识是否与配置引用一致；
  • 优先排查排序和运行模式假设；
  • 用最小可复现组合重现问题；
  • 输出结构一旦变化，文档和测试必须同步更新。

docs.title: 故障排查表
docs.text: 现象 常见原因 首先检查 构造时失败 参数无效 结构校验和语义校验 下游拿不到输出 模块 id 不对或未写入上下文 module_id 与输出映射 组合被拒绝 顺序或类型缺失 校验规则 不同模式行为不一致 隐含执行假设不兼容 运行模式说明

docs.title: 日志建议
docs.text: 优先在宿主应用中使用结构化日志。模块自身应暴露足够的诊断状态，但不应强绑定到某一种日志后端。

docs.title: 发布门槛
docs.text: 如果测试、示例和文档中的参数名、输出结构或兼容性描述不一致，该模块不应发布。

docs.title: 为什么需要校验
docs.text: 平台在运行前验证模块组合的结构正确性，以便尽早、统一地发现配置错误，而不是把问题留到运行时才暴露。

docs.title: 标准执行顺序
docs.text:
批准的模块顺序如下：

  1. indicator
  2. signal
  3. filter
  4. risk
  5. position
  6. execution
  7. output
  8. portfolio

这个顺序反映了从数据推导、决策形成、风险约束、仓位决策、执行桥接到结果输出的依赖流向。

docs.title: 面向实盘的组合
docs.text:
实盘组合至少满足：

  • 至少一个指标模块；
  • 至少一个信号模块；
  • 至少一个仓位模块；
  • 恰好一个执行模块；
  • 执行模块必须位于所有仓位模块之后；
  • 不允许顺序违规。

docs.title: 面向回测的组合
docs.text: 回测模式同样要求顺序合法。如果存在执行模块，它必须是平台批准的仿真型执行模块，而不能依赖真实执行基础设施。

docs.title: 准备层行为
docs.text: 在校验完成前，准备层可能会对模块进行顺序规范化，也可能在批准范围内补充默认执行模块。模块作者不应依赖这些默认行为，示例文档中应始终显式写出完整模块集合。

docs.title: 常见错误
docs.text:
• 把过滤模块放到信号模块之前；
  • 假设仓位模块能先于指标计算运行；
  • 在同一个组合里放多个执行模块；
  • 实盘组合缺少仓位模块；
  • 在回测示例中混入实盘专属执行假设。

docs.title: 发布前检查
docs.text:
• 模块类型声明是否和职责一致；
  • 示例中的模块顺序是否标准；
  • 上游依赖是否写清楚；
  • 输入缺失时行为是否写明；
  • 运行模式兼容性是否有明确声明。

docs.title: 核心术语
docs.text: 模块 实现平台契约的可复用策略构件。 模块类型 用于决定模块在组合中职责和校验方式的类别声明。 上下文 模块共享的运行时对象，承载当前数据、中间结果和模块输出。 组合 按顺序排列并组装成一个策略定义的模块集合。 注册中心 负责模块发现、解析与实例化的受控边界。 准备层 在校验完成前，负责顺序规范化和批准默认补全的阶段。 校验 用于确认模块集合对目标运行模式结构正确、语义可接受的一组检查。 运行模式 模块面向的执行上下文，例如实盘导向或回测导向。 契约测试 验证模块是否遵循公开扩展面，而不只是测试其内部业务逻辑的测试方式。 公开 API 边界 允许外部模块开发者依赖的契约与行为集合。

docs.title: 边界声明
docs.text: 本门户只记录已经批准给模块开发者使用的扩展面。任何未列入该范围的内容，都必须视为内部实现。

docs.title: 模块基类契约
docs.text:
可公开内容包括：

  • 模块元数据字段；
  • 参数模式约定；
  • 生命周期方法；
  • 指标与元数据访问器；
  • 共享上下文的使用方式。

docs.title: 注册中心相关概念
docs.text:
可公开内容包括：

  • 注册；
  • 别名支持；
  • 发现与解析概念；
  • 安全实例化预期。

docs.title: 面向作者的发现规则
docs.text:
• 模块名称必须稳定、可读，并且适合在配置中被引用。
  • 别名只用于兼容性，不应用来替代正式名称。引入别名时，规范名称仍需保留在文档中。
  • 只有当模块通过宿主应用批准的注册或发现路径暴露出来时，才算“可发现”。
  • 动态发现是否开启可能因部署环境不同而变化，模块作者不能假设所有环境都支持自动发现。

docs.title: 标识与输出规则
docs.text:
• module_id 在同一个策略定义中应保持稳定。
  • 需要供下游消费的输出必须写入可预测的键。
  • indicator_ref 这类下游引用应始终指向文档化的模块标识，而不是依赖隐式顺序。
  • 如果模块输出结构发生变化，这属于契约变更，必须做版本和文档同步。

docs.title: 校验相关概念
docs.text:
可公开内容包括：

  • 标准排序；
  • 实盘与回测的组合要求；
  • 会影响示例和文档的准备层概念。

docs.title: 受控扩展区域
docs.text: 执行类扩展不是默认公开定制路径。相较于指标、信号、过滤、风险、sizer、仓位、输出和组合模块，它受到更强的评审、校验和运行约束。

docs.title: 内部专属内容
docs.text:
以下主题刻意不在本网站展开：

  • 专有执行流程内部细节；
  • 基础设施容器具体实现；
  • 实盘适配协议；
  • 状态持久化机制；
  • 系统级风险执行逻辑；
  • 运维阈值和生产调优信息。

docs.title: 如何申请边界调整
docs.text:
如果某个模块团队需要把当前内部能力升级为公开契约，应提交文档治理申请，至少包含：

  1. 使用场景；
  2. 建议公开的契约形式；
  3. 安全性与稳定性影响；
  4. 向后兼容预期。

任何团队都不应在未经批准的情况下，把内部代码片段直接作为外部指导文档发布。
